messages:
emma: Quick onboarding question — before I start next week: can I roll my old 401(k) or an IRA into Redwood's plan? Also, does the plan allow 401(k) loans and when does the company match vest? Lastly, I have an HSA with a different custodian, can that be transferred or do I need to open a new one? cc @raj @jen

raj (People Ops): Congrats and welcome! :tada: Short answers: yes to rollovers (401k or IRA), the plan permits participant loans, and our match vests on a graded schedule. HSA transfers are possible trustee-to-trustee. I'll drop details below.

jen (Benefits): Rollover notes: we accept trustee-to-trustee transfers or a rollover check payable to "Redwood Plan Trustee." For IRA -> 401(k) rollovers, be aware of Roth conversion consequences if the IRA is a Roth. Please upload rollover docs to Workday > Benefits > Documents. Suggested filename: `emma-rollover-<oldplan>-pdf`. Our team reviews uploads within 3 business days.

jen (Benefits): HSA specifics: we support trustee-to-trustee HSA transfers to our HSA custodian. If your current custodian requires forms, ask them for an HSA trustee transfer form and DM me the custodian name so I can confirm payer details. Note: if you took distributions from your personal HSA, those are not rolloverable.

tom (Payroll): Loan mechanics + match timing: - Participant loans allowed up to lesser of $50k or 50% of vested account balance. Loan setup typically takes 1-2 payroll cycles. Repayments come out via payroll deduction once loan paperwork is processed. - Match: elective deferrals start on your first applicable paycheck after enrollment; employer match is calculated each payroll and is based on eligible deferrals going forward (past balances don't retroactively change match). Payroll cutoff reminder: enroll in Workday before the 5th of the month 23:59 PT for the following payroll cycle.

raj (People Ops): Vesting schedule: graded over 4 years at 25% per year starting from your hire date (so after 1 year you're 25% vested, etc.). If you have prior service with Redwood that's recognized, that counts toward vesting. For leaves of absence, the plan SPD has specifics; short paid leaves don't pause service accruals generally, unpaid LOAs longer than 6 months may affect service. See SPD link in Benefits docs or DM me if you want the excerpt.

jen (Benefits): Other practicals: - Loan origination/administration fees are set by our recordkeeper (usually ~$50) and will be charged to the account/paid from the balance per the recordkeeper's policy. - FSA balances do NOT transfer between employers; check your previous plan's grace/runout rules.

hr-bot: Onboarding checklist updated: `401k rollover` step added, `HSA transfer` reminder set for day 1, `Benefits enrollment` email scheduled immediate after account activation. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/onboarding

emma: Thanks — couple quick follow-ups: if I roll an IRA in but it has both pre-tax and after-tax basis, any extra paperwork? Also if I take a loan and then leave, how are outstanding loans treated at separation?

jen (Benefits): If the IRA has after-tax basis (non-deductible contributions), we need Form 8606 info to track basis/avoid double tax on distributions; usually best to roll pre-tax portions to the 401(k) and consult a tax advisor for mixed-basis IRAs.

tom (Payroll): Loan at separation: outstanding loan balances are typically treated per plan doc — either you have a short period to repay, or the loan is treated as a distribution and may be taxable and subject to early withdrawal penalty if under 59½. We follow the plan's standard; if you think you might separate with an outstanding loan, DM payroll so we can outline options.

raj (People Ops): I'll echo the DM offer — upload your rollover PDF and HSA transfer form and I'll confirm receipt + estimated completion date. If you want me to pull the SPD excerpt for leave/vesting, say so. :+1:

emma: Uploading the rollover paperwork now and DM'ing @jen the HSA custodian. Appreciate all the clarity!
